title: cairn.config.json
description: Per-repo cairn configuration. Hand-edited. Lives at the repo root, never inside _cairn/.

hosts.description: Agent hosts cairn writes files for. Every host reads the shared ai/ docs. `claude` adds .claude/ (commands and the code-scout subagent, plus the .mcp.json entry); `codex` adds Codex skills in .agents/skills/, a root AGENTS.md pointer and, when `claude` is not also listed, .agents/code-scout.md. A repo without `claude` gets no .claude/ folder.

docs.description: Knowledge about the project that lives outside ai/contexts/, such as an existing docs folder. cairn lists these in ai/AGENTS.md and the role agents read the ones that cover the task's area; it never parses them.

anyOf.description: A path relative to the repo: a file, or a folder.

path.description: Relative to the repo root: a file, or a folder.

about.description: What the doc covers, in a few words.

when.description: When an agent should read it, e.g. 'a backend domain, service or DAO changes'.

codexSkills.description: Deprecated spelling of adding `codex` to `hosts`; still honoured.

cairn.description: Version of @stonepandastudio/cairn this repo is pinned to.

stack.description: Framework first, then composable add-ons. `cohort: "stack"` in the doctor groups by the first entry; the v2 renderer layers one preset per entry, in order. A bare or comma-separated string is also accepted.

workspace.description: Path, relative to this repo, of the workspace `repos.json` listing this repo and its siblings. Defaults to `../repos.json`. When found (and this repo is listed in it), the rendered ai/AGENTS.md gains a Workspace table and the architect must account for the sibling repos.

model.description: Recommended tier for the reviewer and QA agents, as a tier name ("sonnet", "opus"). Rendered as "Sonnet or higher", so no model version appears in generated files; a versioned id such as "claude-sonnet-5" is still read, with the version dropped.

commands.description: Commands the agents run, when the repo's own differ from what they would look up. Each is optional; an agent that has none finds the command itself in package.json or the README.

build.description: The build command the developer runs before reporting completion, e.g. "npm run build" or "yarn build".

tdd.description: Test-first execution in the main workflow. When true, the architect orders each step's test files before the code and marks every test file unit or integration, and the developer runs red, then green, for each unit file and reports both. The QA backfill agents are unaffected: they write tests for code that already exists.

sizing.description: Opt-in size check. When present, the architect estimates a step's size during `enrich_description` (files touched, lines of code, from the nearest analogs), proposes a split into smaller steps if it is over a limit, and re-checks the real file list in `plan_task`. The estimate is a prediction by the agent, not a measurement; the user decides whether to split. `{}` turns it on with the defaults.

maxLoc.description: Lines of code (created plus changed) above which a step should be split.

maxFiles.description: Files created plus modified above which a step should be split.

validationStack.description: Only meaningful when "nestjs" is in `stack` — ignored otherwise. Selects which presets/nestjs/variants/validation-stack/<name>/ slot set fills code-guidelines.md's DTO/validation sections.

projectKey.description: Required unless provider is "none". For youtrack, falls back to YOUTRACK_PROJECT in .env.

issueTypes.description: jira-server only, except `epic`, which youtrack also reads (the Type value of an epic). YouTrack has no Task/Sub-task type split.

epic.description: Only used by epic commands. Optional.

publicRefs.description: Opt in to public refs: epics get CI-E1, stories created or moved under an epic get CI-<epic>-<n>. Stored as a `ref-<ref>` label/tag; the tracker's own key (CI-79) is unchanged and every tracker command accepts either form.

epicLinkField.description: jira-server only. Custom field id of "Epic Link" (e.g. customfield_10008). Optional: looked up by name the first time an epic command needs it. Set it so `get` can also report a story's epic.

epicNameField.description: jira-server only. Custom field id of "Epic Name". Optional; looked up by name when creating an epic.

statuses.description: Board stage names. `inProgress` is where `enrich_description` moves the issue and `review` is where `code_review` moves it (at the start of the review); a step moves an issue only if you set its stage here. A stage the board does not have is skipped with a message, not an error. Check with `cairn tracker check-statuses`; list the board's stages with `cairn tracker list-statuses`.

inProgress.description: Stage `enrich_description` moves the issue to. Not moved unless set.

review.description: Stage `code_review` moves the issue to, at the start of the review. Not moved unless set.

env.description: Path, relative to the repo root, of the file holding tracker credentials.

envPrefix.description: Prepended to every credential var the provider reads (e.g. "CAIRN_" → CAIRN_YOUTRACK_TOKEN). Set it only when the repo's own app reads JIRA_*/YOUTRACK_* and the names would collide.

agents.description: Role -> agent mapping. Read by the doctor's normalizer today; rendered into command stubs in v2.

model.description: Only read for the `scout` entry: the tier of the code-scout subagent. An alias, never a versioned id, so it follows the latest model of that tier ("inherit" uses the session's model). Default "haiku"; use "sonnet" for a large or unusual tree, where a cheaper model is likelier to report a false "not found".
